title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 4 (Waiver of right to object)

content.overview: Section 4 embodies waiver of the right to object. A party who knows that a derogable Part I provision or an arbitration-agreement requirement has not been complied with, yet proceeds without timely objection, is deemed to have waived the right to object.
content.glance: Knowledge + continued participation + failure to object in time = waiver of that objection.
content.study: Establish knowledge of the non-compliance, continued participation, and failure to object without undue delay or within any prescribed period. Waiver is tied to the particular non-compliance.

sections.heading: Statutory trigger
sections.body: Applies where the party knows of non-compliance with a derogable Part I provision or an arbitration-agreement requirement.

sections.heading: Continued participation
sections.body: The party must nevertheless proceed with the arbitration.

sections.heading: Failure to object in time
sections.body: Objection must not be delayed beyond undue delay or any prescribed period.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.body: The party is deemed to have waived the right to object to that non-compliance.

examples.title: Known non-compliance without objection
examples.body: A party knows a contractual procedural requirement was skipped, continues, and does not object in time. Section 4 may deem waiver.

examples.title: Prompt objection
examples.body: A party objects immediately on learning of the non-compliance. Waiver under s. 4 is not established merely by later participation after objection.

hypotheticals.question: Does participation alone waive every objection?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 4 requires knowledge, a qualifying non-compliance, continued proceedings and failure to object in time.

misconceptions.trap: Any participation automatically waives every objection.
misconceptions.correction: Prove knowledge, qualifying non-compliance, continuation and untimely failure to object.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the section 4 test?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Knowledge of a qualifying non-compliance, continued participation, and failure to object without undue delay or within the prescribed period.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Apply the sequence element by element.

enhancement.definition: Section 4 deems waiver of the right to object where a party knowing of a qualifying non-compliance proceeds without timely objection.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Knowledge + continuation + untimely silence = waiver of that objection.

shortAnswer.answer: Deemed waiver of the right to object to a known qualifying non-compliance if the party proceeds without timely objection.

tenMark.point: Identify the non-compliance and whether the provision is derogable
tenMark.application: Waiver applies only where the party may derogate from the provision.
Actual or constructive knowledge is required before waiver attaches.

tenMark.point: Show continued participation without timely objection
tenMark.application: Silence after knowledge can amount to waiver under s. 4.

tenMark.point: State the consequence of waiver for later challenges
tenMark.application: A waived objection cannot ordinarily be revived at the setting-aside stage.

sixteenMark.point: Explain the policy of section 4 waiver
sixteenMark.application: Prevents tactical silence and protects procedural economy.

sixteenMark.point: Apply the knowledge and participation tests to the facts
sixteenMark.application: Sequence knowledge, continued participation and timing of objection.

sixteenMark.point: Distinguish mandatory provisions from derogable ones
sixteenMark.application: Mandatory protections may limit the reach of waiver.
Ask whether the ground was available and waived earlier.
Waiver does not cure lack of a valid arbitration agreement where the statute so requires.
